A tester's 100+ processes: what leaks, and what's fixed

brindle never stops processes itself. The suspended zsh/eval shells are Claude Code's Bash-tool shells, left behind by Claude CLIs that brindle started. Two leaks leave processes alive. Two sources spawn too many, which is what Defender keeps inspecting. The fixes are in review on fix/process-leaks-and-spawn-rate.

Leak L1: how a shell gets orphaned (in 0.6.3)

All findings

L1Orphaned Bash-tool shells fixed

The window closes before the processes are stopped, so Claude Code's shells outlive their CLI forever, some of them suspended. This matches the tester's report. It's in 0.6.3.

Fix: stop first, then close, on every stop path.

L2Learned-rules claude -p past its time limit fixed

A timeout killed only the CLI; its MCP servers and shells kept running. In 0.6.3.

Fix: it runs in its own process group and is cleaned up whole, with no tools or MCP servers.

S1Idle sync and drift git storm added today fixed

Today's #416 ran 14 git processes per session every 5 seconds, even with nothing changed. It's in build 140, which you're running. Not in 0.6.3.

Fix: git runs only when a session's refs have moved, so 0 at idle.

S2Each sidebar's own git not fixed yet

Every open sidebar runs its own git refreshes and cull: about 60+ processes a minute here. In 0.6.3 too.

Next: share that work across sidebars, the way S1 now does in the daemon.

The daemon's own git, counted exactly per sweep. Each sidebar's git (S2) comes on top of this in every version: about 60+ a minute measured here.

Checked and found sound

Paused, done, closed and culled agents: none of the 49 on this Mac had a process left. Reviewers and auditors, the brindle mcp servers of ended sessions, tmux panes, and reads with timeouts all look sound.

What's left

  • Orphans that already exist aren't cleaned up, because they name no agent and can't be safely matched to one. The tester needs to restart their Mac once after updating to 0.6.4.
  • Sidebar git (S2) is the next spawn source to cut.
  • Each live Claude CLI brings its own MCP servers, a shell snapshot and caffeinate. That scales with how many agents run, and reported workers keep theirs for 30 minutes.

Status: in review, past its second round and converging. It's the last thing 0.6.4 needs. Counts come from this Mac. I haven't seen the tester's machine; their ps output would confirm L1.
